finding.claim: Stored SSRF: attacker-supplied callbackUrl is saved without any validation and later used as the target of server-side POST requests, allowing requests to internal hosts, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), localhost, or arbitrary schemes/ports. The payload is attacker-influenced only indirectly, but the response is not returned; this is mostly blind SSRF, though the request itself reaches internal services.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives attacker-controlled URL from POST /subscribe body
URL stored unvalidated in static subscriptions map
URI.create(cb) builds request URI with no scheme/host/IP allowlist
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP check, or DNS-resolution check anywhere on the path. No authentication visible in this file. HttpClient default does not follow redirects, which does not mitigate direct internal targets.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 builds URI.create(cb) and calls client.send with no scheme/host/IP check; the only regex guard (line 30) protects thumb(), not this path. No auth or routing code exists elsewhere in the repo, so the HTTP exposure of subscribe() rests on the comment at line 12.
